Wrapped Texture Editor - test build
===================================

This build writes a crash report when it crashes.

Before you start: save your work and close any Wrapped Texture Editor that
is still open (also older copies). Then try the three ways of starting it
below, one after the other:

  1. "Wrapped Texture Editor.exe"            (normal start, Vulkan)
  2. "Start - DirectX 12.cmd"                (uses DirectX 12 instead of Vulkan)
  3. "Start - Vulkan without overlays.cmd"   (Vulkan, but without the OBS /
                                              Steam overlay hooks)

In each one, do what used to crash:
  - File > New from Model..., open an OBJ, glTF/GLB or FBX model, click Create
    (models without UVs now open too: the app generates a texture layout)
  - click "Split" (top of the view)
  - paint on the model for a bit, switch between 3D / 2D / Split

Note which of the three crash and which keep working.

Exporting layers (new in this build)
------------------------------------
  - Layers panel: Ctrl-click adds or removes a layer from the selection,
    Shift-click selects a range; a plain click selects just that layer.
  - Right-click a layer > "Export this layer..." (or "Export selected
    layers... (N)" with several selected): the Export dialog opens with
    Layers = "Selected (N)" and writes only those layers.
  - In File > Export..., tick "Pack into one .zip file" to get everything
    as one <name>.zip instead of loose files.

Objects (new in this build)
---------------------------
Open a model made of several parts, e.g. the chess set ABeautifulGame.glb,
or File > Open Sample > "Three Objects".
  - The side panel's "Objects" tab lists the parts. A click selects one,
    Ctrl-click adds or removes, Shift-click selects a range; a double-click
    selects it and moves the camera to it.
  - With the Navigate tool (top of the toolbar), a click on a part in the
    3D view selects it (a drag still turns the camera). Selected parts get
    a light blue tint while the Objects tab is open or Navigate is active.
  - The eye at the left of a row hides or shows that part. Hidden parts
    are not drawn, and painting, stamps and text go "through" them onto
    what is behind.
  - Keys: H = hide the selected parts, Shift+H = show only the selected
    parts (isolate), Shift+F = frame the selected parts, F = frame
    everything that is visible.
  - Alt+H = show everything again. Please check: does Windows beep or
    open a menu when you press Alt+H? (If it does, tell me; Ctrl+Shift+H
    would be the replacement.)
  - Save the project with a part hidden and open it again: the part is
    still hidden and a message says so. Undo is not affected by hiding.
  - Selecting a part never limits where you can paint.

Side panel tabs (new in this build)
-----------------------------------
  - The right panel now has two tab rows: on top Tool | Color |
    Texture sets | Objects, below Layers | Brush | Text.
  - The colour picker is on the "Color" tab. A click on the big colour
    square in the toolbar (left) opens that tab. Changing tools keeps
    the tab you chose.
  - Drag the line between the two groups to give one more room; a
    double-click on that line puts it back to automatic.
  - Close and restart the app: the tabs and the split you chose are kept.
  - Try a small window too (e.g. half the screen): nothing should overlap,
    the pages scroll.

Stickers, part 1: the Sticker tab (new in this build)
-----------------------------------------------------
The side panel has a fifth tab, "Sticker" (at the normal panel width the
tabs stand in two rows: Tool | Color | Texture sets, then Objects |
Sticker; widen the panel and they fit one row).
  1. Place an image with the Stamp tool and a text with the Text tool.
     Select the image (Transform tool), open the Sticker tab, click
     "Classic sticker": the picture gets a white die-cut border and a soft
     shadow on the model; its box (the Transform frame) stays where it was.
     Select the text and do the same; tick "Stroke": a dark line runs
     around the border. Each click is one Undo step.
  2. Open a style block with its small arrow and drag a slider (Width,
     Size...): the model follows while you drag; one Undo takes the whole
     drag back. Untick a block and tick it again: your numbers are kept.
  3. Copy Style on one stamp, select two other stamp layers in the Layers
     list (Ctrl-click), Paste Style: both get it, one Undo removes it from
     both. Clear Style removes every style.
  4. Tray: "From picture..." makes a sticker of a picture file; click it in
     the tray (the Stamp tool is chosen), click on the model twice: two
     stamps show the same sticker. "New Sticker" makes a blank one.
  5. Stamp tool, Tool tab: "Edit before placing" opens the picture in the
     Sticker view before you place it ("Not placed yet" below); add a
     layer, press Done, click on the model: the stamp shows the edited
     picture. The "Style" list there gives new stamps a style right away.
  6. With two stamps of the same sticker (step 4), open one in the Sticker
     view (Edit Sticker) and move a layer with the arrow keys: you are
     asked "This picture is used by 2 stickers." - "Edit all" changes both
     stamps, "Only this one" gives this stamp its own copy first (the other
     stays as it was), Cancel changes nothing.
  7. In the Sticker view the Tool tab has "Layer styles" for the active
     layer (the same blocks and presets).
  8. Export Picture... (Sticker tab or tray) saves a PNG of the finished
     picture, with its border and shadow.
  9. Save, close, open the project again: styles, tray stickers and the
     two stamps are as you left them.
 10. A project made with v0.3.0 (no stickers) opens and exports exactly as
     before.

Stickers, part 2: painting in the Sticker view (new in this build)
------------------------------------------------------------------
Select a placed image stamp and press 4 (or Edit Sticker) to open the
Sticker view: the sticker on the left, the model on the right.
  1. Layers tab: "New" adds an empty layer. Press B (Brush) and paint on
     the canvas: the paint appears under the pointer without delay and the
     model follows while you paint (a little behind). One Ctrl+Z takes the
     whole stroke back. Size, hardness, opacity and flow are in the Tool
     tab ([ and ] change the size); the colour is the primary colour.
  2. E (Eraser) erases on the active layer. Esc while the button is still
     down cancels the stroke; Ctrl+Z while painting takes back only that
     stroke.
  3. Give the layer "Classic sticker" (Tool tab > Layer styles) and paint
     on it: while you paint the canvas shows the new paint without its
     border and the header says "styles update when you lift"; when you
     lift, the white border and the shadow appear around the new paint on
     the canvas and on the model.
  4. G (Fill): click on a colour area of the layer: it is filled with the
     primary colour (Tolerance, Contiguous and Anti-alias in the Tool tab).
     Shift+G (Gradient): drag across the layer; the options choose primary
     to secondary, primary to transparent or your own stops, and Reverse.
  5. I (Eyedropper): click on the sticker to take its colour.
  6. Tool tab > Mask: "Add mask", then paint with black to hide and white
     to show ("Paint on mask" is on); Invert, Apply and Delete do what they
     say, each one Undo step.
  7. Convert a text stamp to a layered sticker and try to paint on its
     text layer: nothing is painted, a message says "Rasterize this layer
     to paint on it" and the header offers "Rasterize"; after it the brush
     paints on the text's pixels and it looks the same as before.
  8. With a pen: pressure makes the stroke thinner or wider; the eraser end
     erases (the tool goes back to the Brush when you turn the pen round
     again); the lower pen button drags the canvas around. With the tablet
     companion, one finger drags the canvas, two fingers zoom, the pen
     paints.
  9. A sticker of a large photo (e.g. 2000 x 2000 pixels): painting stays
     smooth; on a layer with Classic sticker the border comes back within
     about a second after you lift.

Stickers, part 3: selections and cut-out (new in this build)
------------------------------------------------------------
Place a photo of an object on a plain (white) background as a stamp, select
it and press 4. The Sticker menu (only in the Sticker view) and the Tool
tab's Selection, Cut-out and Filter blocks hold the same commands.
  1. M (Marquee): drag a box; a dashed outline shows the selection. Shift
     while pressing adds, Alt subtracts, both intersect (or pick New / Add /
     Subtract / Intersect in the Tool tab). Ellipse, Feather and Fixed
     aspect are in the Tool tab. A click without a drag drops the selection.
  2. L (Lasso): drag to draw freehand; or click corners and close with a
     double-click, a click on the first corner, Enter or "Close lasso".
     Esc drops an open lasso.
  3. W (Magic Wand): click the background: it is selected (Tolerance,
     Contiguous, Anti-alias, "Sample all layers" in the Tool tab).
     Ctrl+A selects all, Ctrl+D none, Ctrl+Shift+I inverts.
  4. With a selection press Delete (or Backspace): the selected pixels of
     the active layer go, one Ctrl+Z brings them back. The stamp itself is
     never deleted. Without a selection Delete only says what to do.
  5. Shift+E (Magic Eraser): click the background: it becomes transparent
     ("Into mask" hides it on a layer mask and keeps the pixels).
  6. Cut-out > Remove Background: a plain background goes in one click and
     the object's soft edge keeps no white rim. On a picture that is
     transparent around already it says so and changes nothing.
  7. Cut-out > Color to Alpha...: a small window opens over the canvas;
     the canvas shows the result while it is open. Pick the colour with
     White / Black / Primary or by clicking the canvas; Apply makes it one
     Undo step, Cancel or Esc changes nothing. Defringe..., Remove White
     Matte and Remove Black Matte clean up edges.
  8. Filter > Blur... and Sharpen...: the same small window with a live
     preview; with a selection only the selected part changes.
  9. Select part of a layer, press V (Move) and drag inside the selection:
     the selected pixels move as a new layer ("Move Selection", one Undo
     step that also brings back the hole). Selection > Layer via Copy /
     Layer via Cut do the same without moving; Crop to Selection makes the
     sticker the size of the selection.
 10. Selection > Grow..., Shrink..., Feather... and Color Range... (click
     the canvas to pick the colour) show the new outline before Apply.
 11. Finally give the stamp "Classic sticker" in the Sticker tab: the model
     shows the cut-out object as a die-cut sticker with a white border that
     follows its edge.
 12. From the tablet companion: every selection mode and command has a
     button (no key or Alt needed); the lasso closes with "Close lasso".

Stickers, part 4: layout, text, shapes and the library (new in this build)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
Select a stamp and press 4. The Sticker menu has two more groups, Sticker
and Layer; the Tool tab has the same buttons at its end.
  1. V (Move): the active layer has a box with eight square handles and a
     round one above it. Drag a corner: the layer scales and keeps its
     proportions (hold Shift to stretch it); drag an edge: one side only;
     drag the round handle: it turns (Shift: 15 degree steps). Each drag is
     one Undo step. The Tool tab shows W, H and Angle to type in, and Flip H,
     Flip V and Reset.
  2. X (Text): click on the canvas: a text layer appears there in the
     primary colour and you can type right away (Esc stops typing). Font,
     size, warp and path are in the Tool tab and the Text tab. Click a text
     layer's letters to edit it again.
  3. U (Shape): drag a box: a shape layer (rectangle, rounded, ellipse,
     polygon, star or line, chosen in the Tool tab) filled with the primary
     colour; Outline uses the secondary colour. With a shape layer active
     the same options change it.
  4. Put a picture layer above a text layer and press Clip in the Layers
     footer (or right-click the row): the picture shows only inside the
     letters.
  5. C (Crop): drag the box's handles or draw a new box; choose Rectangle,
     Rounded or Ellipse; Enter (or Apply crop) crops. The sticker on the
     model stays where it was: only the part outside the box goes.
  6. Sticker > Trim, Add Padding..., Canvas Size...: the artboard changes,
     the artwork stays put on the model. Resize... 200 % makes the sticker
     sharper without making it bigger on the model. Rotate 90 CW / CCW /
     180 and Rotate... turn it on the model too; Flip mirrors it.
  7. Layer > Merge Down (Ctrl+M) and Sticker > Flatten join layers; the
     look does not change, also for two pattern layers clipped to the same
     text. Merge Down refuses a hidden layer (show it first). Every one of
     these is one Undo step.
  8. Adjustments (Tool tab, under Layer styles): Add adjustment... >
     Brightness / Contrast, Hue / Saturation, Levels, Invert, Black & White,
     Posterize or Threshold; the sliders change the layer's look live and
     never its pixels; Remove takes it away again.
  9. Sticker tab > Library: "Choose folder..." (or use the default folder
     in %APPDATA%\WrappedTextureEditor\stickers). Select a tray sticker and
     press "Save to Library": its thumbnail appears under Library. Open
     another model and click the thumbnail: the sticker is in the tray and
     the Stamp tool places it.
 10. Sticker > Export as PSD...: a .psd with the sticker's layers that
     Photoshop or PhotoCraft opens (no link is made).
 11. A text stamp: the Sticker tab's "Convert to layered sticker" turns it
     into a sticker whose text stays editable.

Working with PhotoCraft (new in this build)
-------------------------------------------
A sticker can be edited in PhotoCraft (v0.2.0 portable or the installed
latest) through a linked PSD file next to your project. WTE never starts
PhotoCraft by itself: only your click on "Edit in PhotoCraft" does, and
WTE never comes to the front, flashes or beeps when PhotoCraft saves.
  1. Select a sticker stamp (or an image stamp) and click "Edit in
     PhotoCraft" (Sticker tab; also the Sticker view's header, the Layer
     menu and a stamp layer's right-click menu).
     - A project that was never saved asks "Save the project first, so the
       linked file has a place next to it." Save..., then it goes on.
     - The first time WTE asks "Where is photocraft.exe?" (the portable
       copy leaves no trace WTE can find); Help > Editor locations...
       changes it later.
     - With Photoshop installed as well, the button reads "Edit in..." and
       the first click asks "Edit in which program?" (Photoshop /
       PhotoCraft / Other program..., and "Always use this one"). After
       that the button names your default editor, and the small "Edit
       in..." button beside it opens the list (any editor for this one
       sticker, Other program..., and "Default: <name>").
     - A picture several stamps show asks "Edit all" / "Only this one"
       first. With "Only this one" the other stamps stay as they are.
     - The file is <project>_links\<sticker>_k<number>.psd; the Sticker tab
       shows "Link: linked", "Editor: PhotoCraft" and the file name.
  2. In PhotoCraft paint on a layer, add a layer, a text or a layer mask,
     move layers, and press Ctrl+S. Within about a second the sticker on
     the model updates (one Undo step "Update Linked Sticker"); its
     placement and its styles in WTE stay. WTE's own text and shape layers
     you did not touch in PhotoCraft are still text and shapes in WTE; a
     PhotoCraft text comes back as a picture layer. Do it again: it updates
     again.
  3. Add a layer effect (stroke, shadow) in PhotoCraft and save: WTE shows
     the finished picture as one layer and a note names the effect; Undo
     brings the layers back.
  4. Ctrl+Z in WTE after an update: the badge says "changed in WTE" and the
     file is not applied again by itself; "Update now" takes it again.
  5. Change the sticker in WTE and also in PhotoCraft (save there): the
     question "Both WTE and PhotoCraft changed <name>." with "Take
     PhotoCraft's version" / "Keep WTE's version" / "Decide later". Keep
     WTE's version (or "Send to PhotoCraft") while PhotoCraft has the file
     open warns first; if PhotoCraft then saves its old picture again, WTE
     asks ("PhotoCraft saved over the changes WTE sent to <name>.") instead
     of updating silently.
  6. Click "Edit in PhotoCraft" twice with the v0.2.0 / portable copy: the
     second time asks "This sticker is already open in PhotoCraft...".
     With the installed build: note whether a second tab opens or the
     first one comes forward.
  7. While a stroke, a drag or a text field in the Sticker view is busy,
     a save in PhotoCraft waits and lands when you let go (the selection
     is dropped, "Updated from PhotoCraft").
  8. Save the project: the PSD file is not rewritten (its date stays); the
     project keeps a copy of it. Close WTE, change the PSD in PhotoCraft,
     open the project again: "Linked sticker <name> changed while the
     project was closed." Update / Ignore. Delete the PSD and open the
     project: WTE puts it back from its copy.
  9. Link a sticker and close WTE without saving: the question names the
     sticker ("Stickers linked to PhotoCraft since the last save: ...").
     Saving in PhotoCraft afterwards breaks nothing; the PSD stays in the
     links folder.
 10. Save As to another folder while PhotoCraft has the file open: the
     link files are copied along and a note says WTE keeps following the
     old file until you close WTE; a Ctrl+S in PhotoCraft still updates.
 11. File > Import Sticker from PSD... (or drop a .psd on the window): the
     file becomes a sticker in the tray, layer by layer; "Import Sticker
     from PSD, Keep Linked..." also follows that file when it changes.
     A file larger than 4096 px comes in as one picture fitted into
     4096 px, and a note says so.
 12. Stay in PhotoCraft (or in a full-screen game) and press Ctrl+S: WTE
     does not come to the front, its taskbar button does not flash and no
     sound plays; a question waits inside WTE's window.
 13. Latest PhotoCraft with "Maximize PSD and PSB File Compatibility" off
     and a layer effect: the badge reads "needs a merged picture" with what
     to turn on; "Convert with PhotoCraft's command-line tool" (when
     photocraft-cli.exe is next to photocraft.exe) is the fallback.
 14. Help > Editor locations...: the programs WTE found for Photoshop and
     PhotoCraft (it only reads the registry), Browse... / Clear for each and
     for another program, and the default editor ("Ask" brings the
     question back). Nothing is started from this window.
 15. A sticker opened in PhotoCraft, then Edit in... > Photoshop: WTE asks
     first ("PhotoCraft may still have this file open. Two programs saving
     the same file overwrite each other.") and "Open in Photoshop anyway"
     makes Photoshop the link's editor: the badge, the buttons and the
     questions name Photoshop from then on.
 16. A paint layer in your editor: select a paint layer (not a stamp, not
     locked) and choose Layer > "Edit Layer in PhotoCraft" (or right-click
     its row in the Layers tab; "Edit Layer in" lists the other editors).
     The file is <project>_links\<layer>_l<number>.psd at the texture's
     size; a note says the layer's opacity and blend mode stay in WTE. The
     Layers tab now shows "Link: linked", the editor, the file and the
     buttons Update now / Send to / Show file in Explorer / Unlink above
     the layer list. Paint in the editor and press Ctrl+S: the layer and
     the model update (one Undo step "Update Linked Layer"). Ctrl+Z, a
     conflict, Save, Save As and reopening work as for a sticker (2-10).
     Stamp, text and locked layers do not offer the command.
 17. Change the canvas size of that file in the editor and save: nothing
     changes in WTE and the layer's badge (and a note) say "<layer> is
     W x H in PhotoCraft; the texture is w x h. Undo the size change in
     PhotoCraft." Undo the size change there and save again: it updates.
     Add a second layer in the editor: with "Maximize Compatibility" on
     the layer gets the finished picture; with it off the badge says
     "needs a merged picture" with what to turn on.
 18. Edit > Paste as New Paint Layer (also a right-click on the Layers
     tab's "New" button): a picture copied in another program (or a PNG
     / PSD file copied in Explorer) becomes a new paint layer above the
     active one. A picture of the texture's size lands as it is; another
     size is scaled to fit (its shape kept) and centred. One Undo step.
What does not come across: WTE's layer styles and stamp styles are not
in the file (WTE adds them again to what comes back); a WTE text or shape
layer you change in PhotoCraft comes back as pixels; PhotoCraft's text,
smart and fill layers come back as pictures; effects, adjustment layers,
groups and other blend modes make the sticker one finished picture; 16-bit
files come back as 8-bit; parts outside the canvas are cut off. There is
no drag from PhotoCraft into WTE: use Ctrl+S on a linked sticker.

Drag, drop, copy, paste (new in this build)
-------------------------------------------
WTE now takes drops itself, so a picture lands where you let it go.
  1. Drag a PNG or JPG from Explorer onto the model in the 3D view: while
     you hover, the 3D view gets a frame and a note "Drop to place the
     picture here"; let go and a stamp sits exactly under the pointer at
     the Stamp tool's size (one Undo step), selected with the Transform
     handles. Over the 2D view it lands on that spot of the texture.
  2. Let go beside the model (or over the side panel): nothing is placed;
     the picture becomes the Stamp tool's picture ("Drop to use the
     picture with the Stamp tool"), as before.
  3. Drag three pictures at once onto the model: the first is placed, the
     other two are in the Sticker tab's tray ("2 more added to the tray").
  4. Drag a picture onto a stamp's row in the Layers list (or onto the
     stamp's picture at the top of the Sticker tab): an image stamp gets
     the new picture; a sticker stamp gets it as a new top layer.
  5. In the Sticker view, drop a picture on the canvas: a new layer
     centred where you let go (also a .psd: its layers; a .wtes: its
     layers).
  6. Drag an image from a web browser (Chrome, Edge, Firefox) onto the
     model: it lands like a file (the browser hands over the picture or a
     file without a path). Note the browser and what happened.
  7. Drop a .wtes sticker file or a .psd on the model: a sticker stamp
     there; anywhere else: a tray sticker for the Stamp tool.
  8. Drag a .wtep project or a model over the window: the whole window
     darkens with "Drop to open", as before; let go and it opens.
  9. Drop a file WTE cannot use (a .txt): a note "Not opened: <name> (not
     a model, project, image, PSD or sticker file)"; nothing changes.
 10. In PhotoCraft, use File > Save As, then drag that file from Explorer
     onto the model (there is no drag out of PhotoCraft itself).
If dropping does nothing at all, the log says "drop target" near the top
(copy %APPDATA%\WrappedTextureEditor\log.txt) and a note says that
dropping files does not work in this run. If Photoshop or another program
runs "as administrator" and WTE does not, Windows blocks drops between them.

Copy and paste (new in this build; also in the Edit menu):
 11. Select a stamp (click it with the Transform tool) and press Ctrl+C.
     Paste it into Paint, PhotoCraft or Photoshop: the picture arrives as
     you see it in WTE, styles (outline, shadow) included. Note whether
     the background is transparent, white or black, and in which program.
 12. Back in WTE press Ctrl+V: nothing is placed yet; the Stamp tool is
     chosen with the picture (for a sticker: the sticker with its styles,
     also in the Sticker tab's tray). Click the model: it is placed there.
 13. Edit > Paste at View Centre: the picture is placed at once in the
     middle of the 3D view (one Undo step).
 14. In another program copy a picture (Snipping Tool, a browser's "Copy
     image", PhotoCraft or Photoshop Ctrl+C), then Ctrl+V in WTE: the same
     as 12. If nothing happens, a note says "Nothing WTE can paste. The
     clipboard offers: ...". Help > Clipboard contents... shows that list
     at any time: please write it down for each program you tried.
 15. Copy a picture file in Explorer (Ctrl+C on the file) and Ctrl+V in
     WTE: the same as 12.
 16. In the Sticker view, select an area (Marquee, M) and press Ctrl+C,
     then Ctrl+V: a new layer with just those pixels in the middle of the
     canvas. Ctrl+X takes the selected pixels out of the layer (one Undo
     step) and puts them on the clipboard.
 17. With no stamp selected and a painted paint layer active, Ctrl+C
     copies that whole layer at texture size; paste it in another program.
 18. Text: copy a sentence in Notepad, click into the Text tool's text
     field in WTE and press Ctrl+V: the sentence appears there (also with
     Shift+Insert). Select text in that field, Ctrl+C, and paste it in
     Notepad. Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V in a text field never copies or pastes a
     stamp.
 19. Hold AltGr and press V on a keyboard that has AltGr (German, French,
     ...): nothing is pasted (AltGr is not Ctrl).

Drag out of WTE (new in this build; with the mouse):
 20. Drag a stamp's row of the Layers list out of the WTE window onto the
     desktop or an Explorer folder: a PNG appears there - the stamp as you
     see it, border and shadow included. Inside the window the same drag
     still reorders the rows, as before.
 21. Drag a paint layer's row onto the desktop: a PNG of the whole layer at
     texture size (the same picture "Export this layer" writes).
 22. In the Sticker tab drag the selected stamp's picture (top left), and a
     sticker of the tray, onto the desktop: a PNG each. In the Sticker view
     drag a row of its Layers list out: that layer as a PNG.
 23. Drag the same things onto PhotoCraft v0.2.0: each opens as a new
     document. Onto the latest PhotoCraft: onto its picture (expected: a new
     layer) and onto its tab strip (expected: opens) - please write down
     what really happens.
 24. Drag them into Photoshop: onto an open picture (expected: placed as a
     layer, Enter confirms) and onto the tab bar (expected: opens as its own
     document). Note what happens.
 25. The "PSD" handle under the stamp's picture in the Sticker tab ("drag to
     your editor: stays linked"): in an unsaved project it asks you to save
     first. Saved: drag it onto PhotoCraft, or onto Photoshop's TAB BAR;
     the linked PSD opens there. Edit, Ctrl+S: the sticker on the model
     updates by itself. After the first such drag a note says that in
     Photoshop it stays linked only when it opened as its own tab (dropped
     on a picture, Photoshop places a copy that is not linked).
 26. Press Esc during a drag out: nothing is dropped. After any drag out the
     next mouse move in WTE drags nothing, and reordering the Layers rows
     still works.
 27. The same drags with the pen (may not work: Windows may end a pen drag
     at once; note what happens). The tablet companion cannot drag out: use
     Copy, Export Picture... or Edit in <editor> there.
Files dragged out are written to %LOCALAPPDATA%\WrappedTextureEditor\dragout
(with a list of them, manifest.json). WTE removes only its own files there,
only when they are older than a day and nobody changed them: a file you
saved there yourself (for example with PhotoCraft's Save As) stays. A drag
you cancel with Esc removes its file at once.

Pen tablets (new in this build)
-------------------------------
With a drawing tablet or pen display (Windows Ink on in its driver):
  1. Hover over the model: the brush ring follows the pen tip exactly
     (no offset, also at the screen edges and on a second monitor) and
     the status bar (bottom right) shows "Pen". In a narrow window the
     status bar may leave "Pen" out; then look at the Pen line under
     Tool tab > Brush options > Pen pressure.
  2. Paint in 3D and in 2D, light to hard: the stroke goes thin to thick
     and the status bar shows the percentage. Fast curved strokes are
     smooth, not polygonal. A stroke starts where the tip touches (no
     dot left at the previous stroke's end).
  3. Tap toolbar buttons, layer rows, tabs, sliders and menus with the
     pen: each tap is one click. Hold the pen still above a toolbar
     button for a second: its tooltip appears.
  4. Tool tab > Brush options > Pen pressure: turn Size off and Flow on:
     the width stays the same and the paint builds with pressure. Size on
     with "min 50 %": light strokes are half as wide.
  5. Turn the pen around: the tool switches to the Eraser and erases;
     turn it back: the previous tool returns. Ctrl+Z after an eraser
     stroke undoes that one stroke.
  6. Hold the lower pen button and touch the tablet, then drag: 3D
     orbits, 2D pans; a tap with the button held on a layer row opens
     the row's menu.
  7. Press and hold the pen still on the model: no ring animation, no
     right-click menu, no ripple when you tap.
  8. Restart the app: the pressure settings are remembered.
  9. If the tablet driver's Windows Ink option is off: confirm there is no
     pressure (strokes stay full width), then Help > Tablet setup >
     Tablet input: WinTab, and check that pressure works and each stroke
     appears once, the eraser end erases, a stroke lifted while moving
     has no fat blob at its end, and the first dab of a stroke is not
     bigger than the rest. (Without a WinTab driver a message says
     Windows Ink is used.) Set it back to Windows Ink afterwards.
 10. Mouse painting feels and looks as before.
 11. Pen display with touch: rest your hand on the screen while drawing.
     If the hand paints or moves things, turn touch off in the driver or
     Windows' "Ignore touch input when I'm using my pen" on.
Please note the tablet model and driver version with anything that does
not work, and send the log (see below).

Tablet companion (Android tablet, desktop side)
-----------------------------------------------
The tablet-side steps and what to expect on the tablet are in the tablet
app's own instructions:
  https://github.com/Maviman/tablet-companion  (docs/HOW_TO_TEST.md)
Install the app on the tablet from
  https://github.com/Maviman/tablet-companion/releases
On the PC (Help > Tablet companion...):
  1. USB: turn "USB cable" on. Without adb the line says "No adb found":
     download Google's platform-tools, unpack, Browse for adb.exe. With
     the tablet plugged in and USB debugging allowed the line says
     "Ready". No console window may flash. A fullscreen game you play
     meanwhile must keep the focus.
  2. Connect from the tablet (USB): the dialog asks "<tablet> wants to
     connect" -> Allow. The status bar chip says "Tablet: <name> (USB)".
     The tablet shows the editor within about 2 s.
  3. Draw with the S Pen in 2D and 3D with light and hard pressure: the
     stroke width follows the pressure as with a desktop tablet.
  4. Hold the S Pen side button and drag: orbit in 3D, pan in 2D, nothing
     painted. Fingers: one-finger drag orbits / pans, two fingers pan,
     pinch zooms; taps on buttons and sliders work.
  5. Draw with the PC mouse while the pen hovers on the tablet, and the
     other way round: whoever pressed first draws, nothing gets stuck.
  6. Cover the editor with another window: the tablet stays live.
     Minimize it: the tablet says so, and is live again on restore.
     Press Fit on the tablet: the window takes the tablet's shape without
     coming to the front; Restore (tablet or dialog) brings the size back.
  7. Pull the cable in the middle of a stroke: the stroke ends cleanly on
     the PC (no stuck button), the chip says "Tablet: waiting"; plug in
     again and the tablet continues by itself.
  8. Wi-Fi: turn "Wi-Fi" on (allow the firewall prompt once, private
     networks), type the code from the dialog on the tablet. Close and
     reopen the tablet app: it connects again without a code.
  9. Bluetooth: pair in Windows Settings once, turn "Bluetooth" on, choose
     the PC on the tablet, Allow. The picture is coarser and slower; the
     strokes are complete.
 10. Forget the tablet in the dialog: the next connection asks again.
 11. Turn every link off: the chip disappears; the editor behaves as
     before (nothing listens).
 12. Windows display scaling at 125 % or 150 %, editor maximized: the
     brush outline and hovered buttons sit exactly under the S Pen tip,
     also near the window corners.
Please note the tablet model, the link and the app versions with anything
that does not work, and send the log (see below).

If it crashes
-------------
You should see a box "Wrapped Texture Editor crashed. A crash report was
saved to ...". The report is in the "crash" folder next to the exe:

  crash\crash-<numbers>.txt    (what happened, in plain text)
  crash\crash-<numbers>.dmp    (a small memory snapshot for debugging)

The log of the last run is here (paste this into Explorer's address bar):

  %APPDATA%\WrappedTextureEditor\log.txt

(If another copy of the app was open at the same time, the log is called
log-<number>.txt in the same folder instead.)

Please send the crash .txt file, the .dmp file next to it, and the log.
The log is overwritten every time the app starts, so copy it before
starting the app again.

If nothing crashes, the log of that run is still useful: it lists which
graphics backend was used and which overlay programs were hooked in.
